name: pumpkin cookies
instructions:
Ginny Dyer's Chewy Pumpkin Cookies (In Bloom Bakery) — I think this is the one I made, with two changes: BUTTER CUT TO 1/2 CUP (an even bar — worked well) and HOMEMADE pumpkin spice (see notes).

MAKES: 18 cookies. Oven 350°F, two parchment-lined baking sheets. No chill time required (10 min in the fridge only if the dough is too sticky to roll).

=== INGREDIENTS (HER QUANTITIES) ===

Spiced sugar (for rolling):
- 1/4 cup (50g) granulated white sugar
- 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice

Cookies:
- 1/2 cup (113g) unsalted butter, softened — MY AMOUNT, an even bar; her original is 3/4 cup (168g) (see notes)
- 1 cup (220g) light brown sugar, packed
- 2 egg yolks, room temperature
- 2 tsp vanilla
- 1/2 cup (122g) canned pumpkin puree (she recommends Libby's; fresh puree discouraged as too wet)
- 1 3/4 cups (219g) all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
- 1 tbsp pumpkin pie spice
- 1/2 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F; line two baking sheets with parchment.
2. DRY THE PUMPKIN — NOT OPTIONAL: spread the puree on a plate, press a paper towel onto it to absorb liquid, and repeat at least four more times, until the 1/2 cup has reduced to about 1/4 cup. (Her FAQ: insufficient drying is the main cause of cakey cookies.)
3. Whisk the dry: flour, 1 tbsp pumpkin pie spice, baking soda, baking powder, salt. Set aside.
4. Mix the spiced sugar (granulated sugar + 1/2 tsp pumpkin pie spice) in a small bowl. Set aside.
5. Cream the softened butter and brown sugar on high, 1-2 minutes, until light and fluffy.
6. Add the egg yolks and vanilla; mix on medium 1-2 minutes until pale and fluffy.
7. Add the dried pumpkin; mix on medium-low to combine.
8. Add the dry ingredients; mix on low JUST until combined.
9. Scoop with a 2-tbsp cookie scoop, roll into balls, roll each ball in the spiced sugar. (Too sticky → 10 min fridge.)
10. Place at least 2 inches apart (~6 per sheet).
11. Bake 12-14 minutes: 12 = really chewy centers, 14 = slightly crispier. Centers look puffy when done and fall/wrinkle as they cool.
12. Cool on the sheet 5 minutes, then rack. Best after at least 15 minutes of cooling.
notes:
Transcribed from In Bloom Bakery (Ginny Dyer), 'Chewy Pumpkin Cookies' — inbloombakery.com/chewy-pumpkin-cookies. I THINK this is the one I made (not fully certain).

=== MY BUTTER ADJUSTMENT — 1/2 CUP, AN EVEN BAR ===

I turned her 3/4 cup (168g) of butter into 1/2 CUP (113g) to make an even bar, and it worked well.

=== HOMEMADE PUMPKIN SPICE — CINNAMON AND ALLSPICE LEAD ===

The pumpkin spice was homemade: a mix of CINNAMON, CLOVES, NUTMEG, and ALLSPICE, to taste. CINNAMON and ALLSPICE were the most influential.

=== WHY THEY'RE CHEWY (HER TECHNIQUE) ===

- ALL BROWN SUGAR in the dough, no granulated (the granulated is only the rolling sugar).
- EGG YOLKS ONLY, beaten pale and fluffy with the butter and sugar.
- THE PUMPKIN IS DRIED — the step the whole recipe hinges on. Cakey results = under-dried pumpkin (or scooped rather than spooned-and-leveled flour).
- 12-minute bake for the chewiest result.

=== STORAGE ===

Airtight up to three days, or freeze up to two weeks.
original_chef: Ginny Dyer (In Bloom Bakery) — Chewy Pumpkin Cookies, with my changes: butter cut to 1/2 cup and homemade pumpkin spice (cinnamon/cloves/nutmeg/allspice).
